what: Round-1 response re-measurement: model operations at the sizes of 10 §5 (scale example, two consecutive release runs) and the reviewer's 10 MB drawing validation in Rust (release) and TypeScript (Node, Vitest).
commands: pnpm --dir desktop exec vitest run src/ipc/c11-r1-adversarial.test.ts --silent=false  (ts-10mb-drawing-node.log)
timeOrigin: each value is std::time::Instant / performance.now() elapsed around one operation (wall clock, ms); no absolute timestamps
caveats: single runs, no warm-up repetitions, background load not controlled

operations whose code did not change this round (documentClone, drawingOwnViews, drawingEntryRawJson) are 1.1-2.6x slower than in reviews/evidence/M1-C1.1/model-scale-windows.json on the same machine, so the machine was more loaded; differences to the C1.1 run are uncontrolled comparisons

an A/B run with the new input pass disabled (same build otherwise, not committed) gave drawing100kParseValidateMs 776-804 vs 989-1036 with it, i.e. about +25% for the schema-directed input pass on the 28.6 MB drawing

diff timings are whole-entry / whole-document diffs; C1.2 limits diffs to touched objects
